definition: Impinge means to encroach or intrude on something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impinge. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impinge should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Late-night messages from the office had begun to impinge on the one hour Vera kept for her cello.
To brush against something is the lightest passing contact — it stops well short of impinge, which presses into space that isn't yours.
Invade goes further than impinge: impinging crowds the edge of someone's territory, while invading storms in and claims it.

To encroach is to advance gradually into territory that is not yours — a hedge creeping over a lot line, meetings inching into lunch. Impinge needs no slow creep: a pressure impinges the moment it crosses the boundary, and it always takes on.

To intrude is to push in where you are not welcome, and a person can do it bodily — stepping into the room, cutting into a line. Impinge stays abstract: forces and pressures impinge on time, rights, or quiet, while the walking, breathing visitor intrudes.

Trespass is the physical, legal cousin: to cross onto land or property unlawfully, a matter for signs and courts. Impinge crosses subtler lines — noise impinges on quiet, rules impinge on rights — where nothing is deeded and no law is broken.
